FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:584  (reply_id=3350491282)
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel the timer when manual navigation stops autoplay**

When an autoplaying carousel uses the default `stop_on_interaction = true`, this branch sets `auto_play_stopped` but returns no `cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer)`; the analogous `GoToPrev` branch has the same problem. Since adapters only tear down the recurring interval when the machine emits a cancellation, clicking Next/Prev leaves the autoplay timer running after the transition settles into `Idle`, causing continuous ignored `AutoPlayTick` dispatches and a leaked interval even though rotation was stopped.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-j =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:747  (reply_id=3350491287)
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resume or stop autoplay after pointer drags**

After `PointerDown` cancels `AutoPlayTimer`, `PointerUp` always transitions to `Idle` and never emits a replacement timer or marks `auto_play_stopped`. In an autoplay carousel, a swipe therefore silently kills rotation when `stop_on_interaction` is false, and with the default `stop_on_interaction` true the state/ARIA still report rotation as active because `auto_play_stopped` remains false while no timer exists.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-l =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:781  (reply_id=3350491290)
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel autoplay when focus pauses the carousel**

When focus enters an autoplaying carousel with the default `pause_on_focus = true`, this branch only flips `auto_play_paused` and leaves the state in `AutoPlaying` without emitting `cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer)`. Adapters will keep the existing interval alive, so keyboard focus users can still have slides advance under focus even though the context says autoplay is paused.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-p =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:958  (reply_id=3350491293)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mark paused autoplay as a polite live region**

This live-region decision ignores `auto_play_paused`, so after `AutoPlayPause` or a focus pause the slide group still gets `aria-live="off"` as long as autoplay is configured. The documented carousel behavior says paused/stopped carousels should announce changes politely; with the current attributes, manually changing slides while paused remains silent to assistive technologies.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-w =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:675  (reply_id=3350491303)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let the start control restart stopped autoplay**

The trigger labels stopped autoplay as `Start automatic slide show` and `on_auto_play_trigger_click` dispatches `AutoPlayResume` when `auto_play_stopped` is true, but this guard rejects that event outright. After `AutoPlayStop` or a `stop_on_interaction` navigation, the visible start control is therefore inert and users have no way to restart rotation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-0 =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:498  (reply_id=3350491309)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp the initial default slide index**

If a caller passes `default_index` greater than or equal to `slide_count`, initialization stores that out-of-range value directly in the bindable. That breaks the machine invariant relied on by connect methods (`current_index < slide_count`), causing outputs like `Slide 100 of 3` and no item marked current until some later event happens to clamp the index.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-3 =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:560  (reply_id=3350491313)
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop autoplay for direct slide jumps too**

Indicator clicks and Home/End keyboard shortcuts dispatch `GoToSlide`, but this transition only updates the index and never applies `stop_on_interaction` or cancels `Effect::AutoPlayTimer`. With the default autoplay options, jumping directly to a slide is a manual interaction that should stop rotation just like Prev/Next; instead the timer keeps running and the carousel resumes advancing after `TransitionEnd`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-6 =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:975  (reply_id=3350491317)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep all visible slides accessible**

For `slides_per_view > 1`, this treats every slide except the leading `current_index` as hidden. For example, with two slides visible at once and index 0, slide 1 is still on-screen but receives `aria-hidden` and `inert`, making visible content unreachable to assistive technologies and keyboard users.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1N-8 =====
FILE: crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:307  (reply_id=3350491321)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable next at the last full page**

When `slides_per_view` is greater than 1, the last valid starting index is before the final slide; e.g. three slides with two visible are already at the end when `current_index == 1`. This check still allows another Next navigation to index 2, so adapters render a partial/blank page and the Next trigger remains enabled past the real boundary.

282	    /// Clamp or wrap an index according to `loop_nav`.
283	    ///
284	    /// When `loop_nav` is `true`, out-of-range indices wrap around modulo the
285	    /// slide count; otherwise they are clamped to the `[0, slide_count - 1]`
286	    /// range.
287	    #[must_use]
288	    pub fn clamp_index(&self, i: isize) -> usize {
289	        let n = self.slide_count.get() as isize;
290	
291	        if self.loop_nav {
292	            ((i % n) + n) as usize % self.slide_count.get()
293	        } else {
294	            (i.max(0) as usize).min(self.slide_count.get().saturating_sub(1))
295	        }
296	    }

299	    #[must_use]
300	    pub fn can_go_prev(&self) -> bool {
301	        self.loop_nav || self.current_index() > 0
302	    }

305	    #[must_use]
306	    pub fn can_go_next(&self) -> bool {
307	        self.loop_nav || self.current_index() + 1 < self.slide_count.get()
308	    }

310	    /// CSS translate percentage for the slide track, given the live viewport
311	    /// extent supplied by the adapter.
312	    ///
313	    /// The agnostic core does not read geometry; the adapter passes the
314	    /// measured viewport extent **along the carousel axis** — width for a
315	    /// [`Orientation::Horizontal`] carousel, height for an
316	    /// [`Orientation::Vertical`] one — so the drag-follow correction can be
317	    /// expressed as a percentage of the track. Returns the percentage the
318	    /// adapter should apply as a `translate` along the carousel axis.
319	    #[must_use]
320	    pub fn track_offset_percent(&self, viewport_width: f64) -> f64 {
321	        let idx = self.current_index() as f64;
322	
323	        let per_slide = 100.0 / self.slides_per_view;
324	
325	        let drag_correction = if viewport_width > 0.0 {
326	            (self.drag_delta / viewport_width) * 100.0
327	        } else {
328	            0.0
329	        };
330	
331	        -(idx * per_slide) + drag_correction
332	    }
333	}

Resolve rotation now the gesture ended:\n                //  - a navigating swipe with `stop_on_interaction` permanently\n                //    stops it (mark stopped; the timer stays cancelled);\n                //  - otherwise, if rotation was still active (not stopped, not\n                //    focus/hover-paused), re-arm the timer so it resumes —\n                //    without this a swipe silently kills rotation, or leaves\n                //    the state reporting \"playing\" with no timer running.\n                let navigated = next_idx.is_some();\n                let stop_on_interaction = ctx\n                    .auto_play\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .is_some_and(|o| o.stop_on_interaction);\n                let mark_stopped = navigated && stop_on_interaction;\n                let resume = ctx.auto_play.is_some()\n                    && !mark_stopped\n                    && !ctx.auto_play_stopped\n                    && !ctx.auto_play_paused;\n\n                let target = if resume {\n                    State::AutoPlaying\n                } else {\n                    State::Idle\n                };\n\n                let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(target).apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    ctx.drag_start_pos = None;\n                    ctx.drag_delta = 0.0;\n                    ctx.swipe_velocity = 0.0;\n                    ctx.drag_last_timestamp = None;\n\n                    if let Some(idx) = next_idx {\n                        ctx.index.set(idx);\n                    }\n\n                    if mark_stopped {\n                        ctx.auto_play_stopped = true;\n                    }\n                });\n\n                if resume {\n                    plan = plan.with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::AutoPlayTimer));\n                }\n\n                Some(plan)\n            }"

  "new_string": "            Event::FocusSlide { index } => {\n                // Clamp to the last valid starting index: a focused slide is a\n                // real slide, but focusing one already inside the visible\n                // window must not push `current_index` past the boundary.\n                let idx = (*index).min(ctx.last_index());\n                let current = ctx.current_index();\n                let should_pause = ctx.auto_play.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| o.pause_on_focus);\n\n                if should_pause {\n                    // Pausing on focus mirrors `AutoPlayPause`: leave\n                    // `AutoPlaying` and cancel the timer so slides do not keep\n                    // advancing under keyboard focus.\n                    let plan = if *state == State::AutoPlaying {\n                        TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle)\n                    } else {\n                        TransitionPlan::new()\n                    };\n                    return Some(\n                        plan.apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                            if idx != current {\n                                ctx.index.set(idx);\n                            }\n                            ctx.auto_play_paused = true;\n                        })\n                        .cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer),\n                    );\n                }\n\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    if idx != current {\n                        ctx.index.set(idx);\n                    }\n                }))\n            }"

  "new_string": "impl Context {\n    pub fn current_index(&self) -> usize { *self.index.get() }\n\n    /// Number of slide slots occupied at once, rounding a fractional\n    /// `slides_per_view` up so a partially visible trailing slide still counts\n    /// as on-screen. Always at least `1`.\n    pub fn visible_count(&self) -> usize {\n        (self.slides_per_view.ceil() as usize).max(1)\n    }\n\n    /// Largest valid starting index for non-looping navigation. With\n    /// `slides_per_view > 1` the last page is flush to the end\n    /// (contain-scroll): `slide_count - visible_count`.\n    pub fn last_index(&self) -> usize {\n        self.slide_count.get().saturating_sub(self.visible_count())\n    }\n\n    /// Clamp or wrap an index according to `loop_nav`.\n    pub fn clamp_index(&self, i: isize) -> usize {\n        let n = self.slide_count.get() as isize;\n        if self.loop_nav {\n            ((i % n) + n) as usize % self.slide_count.get()\n        } else {\n            (i.max(0) as usize).min(self.last_index())\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn can_go_prev(&self) -> bool { self.loop_nav || self.current_index() > 0 }\n    pub fn can_go_next(&self) -> bool { self.loop_nav || self.current_index() < self.last_index() }\n\n    /// Whether `index` is within the visible window of `visible_count` slides\n    /// starting at `current_index` (wrapping when `loop_nav` is set). Slides\n    /// outside the window are hidden from assistive technology.\n    pub fn is_slide_visible(&self, index: usize) -> bool {\n        let current = self.current_index();\n        let count = self.slide_count.get();\n        (0..self.visible_count()).any(|offset| {\n            let slot = if self.loop_nav { (current + offset) % count } else { current + offset };\n            slot == index\n        })\n    }"
}

  "new_string": "pub struct Machine;\n\n/// Build the transition for a manual navigation to `idx`: enter\n/// `Transitioning` and set the index, and — when `stop_on_interaction` is\n/// configured — permanently stop auto-play and cancel its timer. The\n/// cancellation is essential: without it the adapter's recurring interval\n/// keeps running after rotation has \"stopped\", leaking the timer and\n/// dispatching ignored `AutoPlayTick`s.\nfn navigate_to(ctx: &Context, idx: usize) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    let stop = ctx.auto_play.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| o.stop_on_interaction);\n    let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Transitioning).apply(move |ctx| {\n        ctx.index.set(idx);\n        if stop { ctx.auto_play_stopped = true; }\n    });\n    if stop { plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer); }\n    plan\n}\n\nimpl ars_core::Machine for Machine {"
}

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1sVC  crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:569  reply=3350661118 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync controlled index changes from props**

When the carousel is used in controlled mode and the parent later calls `Service::set_props` with a new `Props::index`, the machine never overrides `on_props_changed`, so the cloned `Bindable` stored here is never updated via `sync_controlled`. In that controlled-signal sync path the rendered active slide, progress text, and indicator selection remain stuck on the initial controlled value until some internal event changes state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1sVI  crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:577  reply=3350661125 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp zero slides_per_move to one**

If a caller passes `slides_per_move: Some(0)`, every navigation path computes a zero step, so `GoToNext`, `GoToPrev`, and auto-play ticks transition without changing `current_index`; with `stop_on_interaction` a manual click can even permanently stop rotation while the slide does not move. Because the public prop is a plain `usize`, normalize this to at least one (or make it non-zero) before storing it in context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1sVM  crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:840  reply=3350661131 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restart autoplay after cancelled drags**

When an autoplaying carousel receives `PointerDown`, the timer is cancelled for the drag, but if the browser then sends `PointerCancel` (for example because touch scrolling or pointer capture is interrupted), this branch only clears drag state and never re-emits `AutoPlayTimer`. The service remains in `AutoPlaying` with `auto_play_stopped == false`, but the adapter has already torn down the interval, so rotation silently stops until some unrelated resume event occurs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1sVP  crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:1191  reply=3350661137 =====
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat missing autoplay config as not playing**

For a carousel with `auto_play: None`, this calculation still reports the autoplay control as playing because both flags default to false, so `auto_play_trigger_attrs()` renders the pause label and `aria-pressed="true"` even though autoplay is disabled and no timer exists. If an adapter or consumer renders the exposed `AutoPlayTrigger` part unconditionally, assistive tech announces a pause control for a feature that is not running.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1sVQ  crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:576  reply=3350661139 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize invalid slides_per_view values**

Because `slides_per_view` is a public `Option<f64>`, callers can pass `Some(0.0)` or another non-positive/non-finite value; storing it directly makes `track_offset_percent()` divide by that value, producing infinite or NaN offsets that adapters will turn into invalid transforms. Clamp or reject values to a finite positive minimum before they enter the context, as is done implicitly for the default case.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G1sVZ  crates/ars-components/src/layout/carousel/mod.rs:693  reply=3350661150 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore autoplay ticks at the final non-looping page**

In a non-looping autoplay carousel already at `last_index()`, `clamp_index(current + step)` returns the same index but this branch still enters `Transitioning`. Since the adapter may not get a CSS `transitionend` when the transform does not change, the machine can become stuck in `Transitioning` and reject manual navigation; guard with `can_go_next()` or keep the machine in a resting state when the tick would not advance.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2HqE  L590  reply=3350813014 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp controlled index during initialization**

When a caller supplies `Props.index`, this path clones the controlled `Bindable` directly and skips the `initial_index` clamp used for uncontrolled mode. With an initial controlled value past `last_index()` (for example `index=100` with 3 slides, or an index beyond the last page when `slides_per_view > 1`), the service starts with `current_index()` out of range before any prop-change sync can run, so no real item is current and `progress_text()` can render values like `Slide 101 of 3`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2HqG  L650  reply=3350813016 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle controlled-to-uncontrolled index changes**

If `Props.index` changes from `Some(...)` to `None`, `old_index != new_index` is true but the `let Some(index) = new_index` guard prevents any event from being dispatched. The context `Bindable` therefore remains controlled by the old value; subsequent `GoToNext`/`GoToSlide` calls only update the pending internal value while `current_index()`, indicators, and progress text keep reading the stale controlled index, so the carousel cannot actually become uncontrolled via `set_props`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2HqH  L653  reply=3350813018 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Synchronize autoplay prop changes**

When a mounted carousel receives new props that only change `auto_play` (for example `Some(...)` to `None`), this falls through with no sync event, so `ctx.auto_play` remains at the old value and any active `AutoPlayTimer` is not cancelled. In that scenario the parent has disabled autoplay, but the old interval can keep dispatching ticks and advancing slides because the machine still believes autoplay is configured.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2HqL  L738  reply=3350813023 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip transitions when wrapped autoplay stays put**

For looped carousels, `can_go_next()` is always true, but `clamp_index(current + slides_per_move)` can still equal the current index, such as with a single-slide carousel or when `slides_per_move` is a multiple of `slide_count`. This enters `Transitioning` without changing the transform, the same missing-`transitionend` case the nearby comment avoids for non-looping boundaries, leaving autoplay stuck in `Transitioning` with future ticks ignored.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2HqP  L674  reply=3350813027 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore direct jumps to the current slide**

When the requested slide clamps to the current index, such as clicking the already-selected indicator or pressing `Home` while on the first slide, this still calls `navigate_to` and enters `Transitioning` even though the track transform does not change. In that no-op case adapters have no real CSS transition to report, so `TransitionEnd` may never arrive and the carousel can remain stuck in `Transitioning`, blocking all subsequent navigation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2HqS  L712  reply=3350813031 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear the paused flag when starting autoplay**

If `Event::AutoPlayStart` is sent after `Event::AutoPlayPause`, this arms `AutoPlayTimer` and moves to `AutoPlaying` but leaves `ctx.auto_play_paused` set. The timer can then advance slides while `auto_play_trigger_attrs()` still reports `aria-pressed="false"` and `item_group_attrs()` uses the paused live-region mode, so adapters using the documented start event expose a paused UI for an actively rotating carousel.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

(Honours the\n                // preserved stopped/paused flags.)\n                let want_timer =\n                    new_auto.is_some() && !ctx.auto_play_stopped && !ctx.auto_play_paused;\n\n                // Only the auto-play transition moves the resting state:\n                // enabling/resuming → AutoPlaying; disabling while playing → Idle.\n                let target = if auto_changed {\n                    if want_timer {\n                        State::AutoPlaying\n                    } else if *state == State::AutoPlaying {\n                        State::Idle\n                    } else {\n                        *state\n                    }\n                } else {\n                    *state\n                };\n\n                let props = props.clone();\n                let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(target).apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    let slides_per_view = props\n                        .slides_per_view\n                        .filter(|value| value.is_finite() && *value > 0.0)\n                        .unwrap_or(1.0);\n\n                    ctx.slide_count = props.slide_count;\n                    ctx.loop_nav = props.loop_nav;\n                    ctx.auto_play = props.auto_play.clone();\n                    ctx.spacing = props.spacing.unwrap_or(0.0);\n                    ctx.slides_per_view = slides_per_view;\n                    ctx.slides_per_move = props.slides_per_move.unwrap_or(1).max(1);\n                    ctx.align = props.align.unwrap_or_default();\n                    ctx.orientation = props.orientation.unwrap_or_default();\n                    ctx.is_rtl = props.is_rtl;\n                    ctx.transition_duration = props\n                        .transition_duration\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| Duration::from_millis(300));\n                    ctx.swipe_threshold = props.swipe_threshold.unwrap_or(50.0);\n\n                    // Track the controlled signal (clamped); `None` returns the\n                    // bindable to uncontrolled mode.\n                    let controlled = props\n                        .index\n                        .as_ref()\n                        .map(|bindable| (*bindable.get()).min(ctx.last_index()));\n                    ctx.index.sync_controlled(controlled);\n\n                    // Keep an uncontrolled index in range if the slide count or\n                    // visible window shrank.\n                    if !ctx.index.is_controlled() {\n                        let clamped = ctx.current_index().min(ctx.last_index());\n                        ctx.index.set(clamped);\n                    }\n\n                    // Without auto-play configured, the play/pause flags are\n                    // meaningless — reset them so the controls read correctly.\n                    if ctx.auto_play.is_none() {\n                        ctx.auto_play_paused = false;\n                        ctx.auto_play_stopped = false;\n                    }\n                });\n\n                // Restart the interval when auto-play config changed so a new\n                // interval/enable takes effect; 307	/// Build the transition for a manual navigation to `idx`: enter
308	/// `Transitioning` and set the index, and — when `stop_on_interaction` is
309	/// configured — permanently stop auto-play and cancel its timer. The
310	/// cancellation is essential: without it the adapter's recurring interval
311	/// keeps running after rotation has "stopped", leaking the timer and
312	/// dispatching ignored `AutoPlayTick`s.
313	fn navigate_to(ctx: &Context, idx: usize) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {
314	    let stop = ctx.auto_play.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| o.stop_on_interaction);
315	    let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Transitioning).apply(move |ctx| {
316	        ctx.index.set(idx);
317	        if stop { ctx.auto_play_stopped = true; }
318	    });
319	    if stop { plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer); }
320	    plan
321	}

  "old_string": "/// dispatching ignored `AutoPlayTick`s.\nfn navigate_to(ctx: &Context, idx: usize) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    let stop = ctx.auto_play.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| o.stop_on_interaction);\n    let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Transitioning).apply(move |ctx| {\n        ctx.index.set(idx);\n        if stop { ctx.auto_play_stopped = true; }\n    });\n    if stop { plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer); }\n    plan\n}",
  "new_string": "/// dispatching ignored `AutoPlayTick`s.\n///\n/// Returns `None` when `idx` equals the current index: the transform would not\n/// change, so the adapter has no CSS transition to report and `TransitionEnd`\n/// may never arrive — entering `Transitioning` would strand the machine.\nfn navigate_to(ctx: &Context, idx: usize) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    if idx == ctx.current_index() { return None; }\n    let stop = ctx.auto_play.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| o.stop_on_interaction);\n    let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Transitioning).apply(move |ctx| {\n        ctx.index.set(idx);\n        if stop { ctx.auto_play_stopped = true; }\n    });\n    if stop { plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer); }\n    Some(plan)\n}"
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard autoplay toggle when autoplay is disabled**

When `auto_play` is `None` (the default), the exposed autoplay trigger still renders as a non-playing “Start” control, but clicking it enters this `else` branch and dispatches `AutoPlayPause`, which sets `auto_play_paused = true`. If the parent later enables autoplay via `set_props`, `SyncProps` computes `want_timer` from that stale paused flag and the timer is not started, so autoplay remains inert until another manual resume; this can happen whenever the trigger is rendered before autoplay is configured.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2-fw  L840  reply=3351116716 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore pointer-up events when no drag is active**

When an auto-playing carousel receives `PointerUp` without a preceding `PointerDown` recorded in `drag_start_pos`, this arm still computes `resume = true` and emits a new `AutoPlayTimer` even though the existing timer was never cancelled. A stray or adapter-level pointer-up on the viewport can therefore create duplicate autoplay intervals; this should no-op unless a drag is active, like the `PointerMove`/`PointerCancel` paths already do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2-f6  L855  reply=3351116729 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply slides_per_move to swipe navigation**

For carousels configured for page-by-page movement, e.g. `slides_per_move: Some(3)`, next/prev buttons and autoplay advance by that step, but a swipe always moves only one slide because this path hard-codes `cur + 1`/`cur - 1`. Since `slides_per_move` is documented as the number of slides to advance per navigation action, touch users get a different carousel position than keyboard/button users for the same component configuration.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2-f-  L958  reply=3351116734 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not scroll when focus enters an already visible slide**

With `slides_per_view > 1`, focusing a non-leading slide that is already in the visible window still sets `current_index` to that slide's index. For example, at `current_index = 0` with two visible slides, tabbing into slide 1 shifts the carousel to start at 1, moving content unexpectedly during normal focus navigation; the focus handler should leave the index alone when `ctx.is_slide_visible(*index)` is already true.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2-gD  L546  reply=3351116743 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Emit an index-change path for controlled carousels**

When `Props.index` is controlled, `Bindable::set` only updates the hidden internal value while `current_index()` continues to read the controlled value, and this props type has no `on_index_change` callback/effect for the parent to round-trip the requested index. In controlled usage, clicking Next/Prev or an indicator therefore enters `Transitioning` but the visible index never changes, so controlled carousels are effectively non-navigable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2-gJ  L770  reply=3351116753 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor pause_on_hover before pausing rotation**

`pause_on_hover` is exposed as part of `AutoPlayOptions`, but the machine never reads it; `AutoPlayPause` pauses any configured auto-play regardless of that setting. When an adapter dispatches the pause event from pointer hover, a carousel configured with `pause_on_hover: false` will still stop rotating, so this option needs a hover-specific event/handler or a guard that preserves manual pause behavior while respecting the hover flag.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G2-gN  L343  reply=3351116758 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable loop controls when there is nowhere to move**

With `loop_nav: true` and a single slide, or when `slides_per_view` already shows all slides, `can_go_prev`/`can_go_next` still return true even though every navigation clamps or wraps back to the same index. The controls therefore render enabled but clicks are no-ops because `navigate_to` rejects the unchanged index; those controls should be disabled when `last_index() == 0` (or otherwise no distinct target exists), even in looping mode.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

fn step_plan(ctx: &Context, step: f64, up: bool) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {
    let current = *ctx.value.get();

    let raw = if up { current + step } else { current - step };

    set_value_plan(ctx, raw, None, true, true, false)
}

fn value_change_effect(value: f64) -> PendingEffect<Machine> {
    PendingEffect::new(
        Effect::ValueChange,
        move |_ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {
            if let Some(callback) = &props.on_value_change {
                callback(value);
            }

            no_cleanup()
        },
    )
}

The carousel spec has the `Bindable` but is missing the matching callback — so Q4 is completing the established pattern. **Q5 (`pause_on_hover`)** is genuinely ambiguous in the spec (`AutoPlayPause` is documented as the "hover/focus" pause yet `FocusSlide` separately gates `pause_on_focus`), so I'll implement Q1–Q4 + Q6 and ask you about Q5.

|ctx: &mut Context| {\n                        ctx.index.set(idx);\n                    })\n                    .with_effect(index_change_effect(idx)),\n                )\n            }"

    #[test]
    fn value_change_callbacks_are_emitted_for_value_and_commit_events() {
        let changes = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let ends = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));

        let captured_changes = Arc::clone(&changes);
        let captured_ends = Arc::clone(&ends);

        let mut svc = service(Props {
            on_value_change: Some(callback(move |value: f64| {
                captured_changes.lock().unwrap().push(value);
            })),
            on_value_change_end: Some(callback(move |value: f64| {
                captured_ends.lock().unwrap().push(value);
            })),
            ..props()
        });

        let mut increment = svc.send(Event::Increment);

        assert_eq!(increment.pending_effects.len(), 2);

        let send: StrongSend<Event> = Arc::new(|_| {});

        for effect in increment.pending_effects.drain(..) {
            drop(effect.run(svc.context(), svc.props(), Arc::clone(&send)));
        }

        assert_eq!(changes.lock().unwrap().as_slice(), &[30.0]);
        assert_eq!(ends.lock().unwrap().as_slice(), &[30.0]);

        let mut drag = svc.send(Event::PointerDown { value: 55.0 });

        assert_eq!(drag.pending_effects.len(), 1);

        for effect in drag.pending_effects.drain(..) {
            drop(effect.run(svc.context(), svc.props(), Arc::clone(&send)));
        }

        let mut end = svc.send(Event::PointerUp);

        assert_eq!(end.pending_effects.len(), 1);

        for effect in end.pending_effects.drain(..) {
            drop(effect.run(svc.context(), svc.props(), Arc::clone(&send)));
        }

        assert_eq!(changes.lock().unwrap().as_slice(), &[30.0, 55.0]);
        assert_eq!(ends.lock().unwrap().as_slice(), &[30.0, 55.0]);
    }

Focusing slide 3 (off-screen) scrolls to the\n        // last full page (index 2).\n        drop(service.send(Event::FocusSlide { index: 3 }));\n        assert_eq!(service.context().current_index(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn loop_controls_disabled_with_single_position() {\n        // Single slide, looping: no distinct target, so both controls disabled.\n        let ctx = service(Props {\n            loop_nav: true,\n            ..props(1)\n        })\n        .context()\n        .clone();\n        assert_eq!(ctx.last_index(), 0);\n        assert!(!ctx.can_go_prev());\n        assert!(!ctx.can_go_next());\n\n        // slides_per_view covering every slide: likewise nowhere to move.\n        let ctx_all = service(Props {\n            loop_nav: true,\n            slides_per_view: Some(3.0),\n            ..props(3)\n        })\n        .context()\n        .clone();\n        assert_eq!(ctx_all.last_index(), 0);\n        assert!(!ctx_all.can_go_next());\n    }\n\n    /// Run every pending effect from `result`, then return the captured values.\n    fn captured_index_changes(service: &Service<Machine>, event: Event) -> Vec<usize> {\n        let changes = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));\n        let captured = Arc::clone(&changes);\n        // The on_index_change callback lives in props; build a fresh service so\n        // the effect can read it. (Caller passes a service already wired.)\n        let mut service = Service::<Machine>::new(\n            Props {\n                on_index_change: Some(callback(move |index: usize| {\n                    captured.lock().expect(\"lock\").push(index);\n                })),\n                ..service.props().clone()\n            },\n            &Env::default(),\n            &Messages::default(),\n        );\n        drop(service.take_initial_effects());\n        let mut result = service.send(event);\n        let send: StrongSend<Event> = Arc::new(|_| {});\n        for effect in result.pending_effects.drain(..) {\n            drop(effect.run(service.context(), service.props(), Arc::clone(&send)));\n        }\n        let values = changes.lock().expect(\"lock\").clone();\n        values\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn controlled_navigation_round_trips_via_on_index_change() {\n        // Controlled carousel: navigation must notify the parent of the\n        // requested index so it can push it back through `Props::index`.\n        let base = service(Props {\n            index: Some(Bindable::controlled(0)),\n            ..props(4)\n        });\n        let changes = captured_index_changes(&base, Event::GoToNext);\n        assert_eq!(changes, vec![1]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn manual_navigation_emits_index_change_effect() {\n        let mut service = service(props(4));\n        let result = service.send(Event::GoToNext);\n        assert!(\n            result\n                .pending_effects\n                .iter()\n                .any(|effect| effect.name == Effect::IndexChange)\n        );\n    }\n}"

300	### 1.5 Full Machine Implementation
301	
302	Auto-play timing is an adapter concern, not an agnostic one: the core never calls
303	`set_interval`/`set_timeout` directly. Instead it emits a typed [`Effect`] marker that adapters
304	dispatch on (`match effect.name { Effect::AutoPlayTimer => … }`) — the same convention used by
305	`toast::single::Effect`, `dialog::Effect`, `popover::Effect`, and `tooltip::Effect`. The adapter
306	resolving `Effect::AutoPlayTimer` runs a recurring interval of `ctx.auto_play.interval` that
307	dispatches `Event::AutoPlayTick`, and tears it down when the effect is cancelled.
308	
309	```rust
310	/// Typed identifier for every named effect intent the carousel machine emits.
311	///
312	/// Adapters dispatch on `effect.name` exhaustively so unhandled variants and
313	/// name typos surface at compile time.
314	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]

328	/// Build the transition for a manual navigation to `idx`: enter
329	/// `Transitioning` and set the index, and — when `stop_on_interaction` is
330	/// configured — permanently stop auto-play and cancel its timer. The
331	/// cancellation is essential: without it the adapter's recurring interval
332	/// keeps running after rotation has "stopped", leaking the timer and

337	/// may never arrive — entering `Transitioning` would strand the machine.
338	fn navigate_to(ctx: &Context, idx: usize) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
339	    if idx == ctx.current_index() { return None; }

607	            Event::PointerUp => {
608	                let delta = ctx.drag_delta;
609	                let velocity = ctx.swipe_velocity;
610	                let threshold = ctx.swipe_threshold;
611	                // A brisk flick (>0.5 px/ms) reduces the distance threshold.
612	                let effective = if velocity.abs() > 0.5 { threshold * 0.3 } else { threshold };
613	
614	                let cur = ctx.current_index() as isize;
615	                let next_idx = if delta < -effective && ctx.can_go_next() {
616	                    Some(ctx.clamp_index(cur + 1))
617	                } else if delta > effective && ctx.can_go_prev() {
618	                    Some(ctx.clamp_index(cur - 1))
619	                } else {
620	                    None
621	                };
622	
623	                // `PointerDown` cancelled the timer for the drag. Resolve
624	                // rotation now the gesture ended: a navigating swipe with
625	                // `stop_on_interaction` stops it; otherwise, if rotation was
626	                // still active, re-arm the timer (resume) — without this a
627	                // swipe silently kills rotation, or leaves the state reporting
628	                // "playing" with no timer running.

630	                let stop = ctx.auto_play.as_ref().is_some_and(|o| o.stop_on_interaction);

641	                    ctx.swipe_velocity = 0.0;
642	                    ctx.drag_last_timestamp = None;
643	                    if let Some(idx) = next_idx {

  "new_string": "- Auto-play pauses on hover (`mouseenter` → `HoverStart`) when `AutoPlayOptions::pause_on_hover` is set, and on focus within the carousel (`focusin` → `FocusSlide`) when `pause_on_focus` is set. Each gate is enforced in the core, not the adapter. Rotation resumes on `mouseleave` / `focusout` (`HoverEnd` / `Blur`) unless permanently stopped. The auto-play trigger button's manual pause (`AutoPlayPause`) is unconditional and independent of these options."
}

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G5n0L  L736  reply=3352078036 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve loop targets for direct slide jumps**

When `loop_nav` is true and `slides_per_view > 1`, this clamps every direct `GoToSlide` target to `last_index()`, even though looped navigation can validly start at wrapped positions beyond that boundary. For example, with 5 slides and 2 visible slides, clicking the indicator for slide 4 dispatches `GoToSlide { index: 4 }` but lands on index 3, so the last indicator can never select its own slide even though `GoToNext` from index 3 can reach index 4.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G5n0P  L913  reply=3352078041 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Leave autoplay state while dragging**

On an autoplaying carousel, `PointerDown` cancels the timer but leaves the state as `AutoPlaying`; if an interval callback was already queued before the cancellation cleanup runs, a subsequent `AutoPlayTick` during the active drag still passes the `state == AutoPlaying` guard and advances the slide under the user's pointer. The drag state should either move out of `AutoPlaying` here or make ticks no-op while `drag_start_pos` is set.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G5n0V  L876  reply=3352078049 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Don't let hover/focus exits restart manual pauses**

Because manual `AutoPlayPause`, hover pause, and focus pause all share the same `auto_play_paused` flag, any later `HoverEnd` (and similarly `Blur`) restarts the timer even when the pause came from the play/pause trigger or when focus is still inside the carousel. For example, a user can click the autoplay trigger to pause rotation, then move the pointer out of the carousel and unexpectedly have rotation resume without pressing Start.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G5n0W  L1640  reply=3352078051 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose pointer-cancel dispatch**

The machine has a `PointerCancel` transition that clears drag state and re-arms autoplay after pointer-capture loss or touch-scroll cancellation, but the connect API only exposes down/move/up handlers. When adapters wire viewport events through this API, a browser `pointercancel` leaves `drag_start_pos` set and the timer canceled until some later pointer-up occurs, so canceled gestures can keep affecting drag offset and autoplay lifecycle.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G5n0X  L1414  reply=3352078054 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Set native button types on carousel controls**

The carousel anatomy renders the prev/next triggers, indicators, and autoplay trigger as `<button>` elements, but these attrs never set `type="button"`. When a carousel is placed inside a form, clicking any of those controls defaults to a submit button in HTML, so slide navigation can unexpectedly submit the surrounding form instead of only changing carousel state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6F4y  L1025  reply=3352246885 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep swipe navigation transitioning until settle**

When a swipe crosses the threshold while autoplay remains enabled with `stop_on_interaction = false`, `PointerDown` has canceled the timer but `PointerUp` immediately returns to `AutoPlaying` and re-arms it instead of entering `Transitioning`. With an autoplay interval shorter than the snap animation, the next `AutoPlayTick` is accepted during that slide transition because `drag_start_pos` is already cleared; button/autoplay navigation avoids this by staying `Transitioning` until `TransitionEnd`. Route swipe navigations through `Transitioning` and resume autoplay after settle so ticks and additional navigation are blocked during the snap.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6F41  L666  reply=3352246888 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve looped starting indices**

For looped multi-view carousels, capping the initial value at `slide_count - ceil(slides_per_view)` makes valid wrapped starts unreachable: e.g. `slide_count = 5`, `slides_per_view = 2`, `loop_nav = true`, and `default_index` or controlled `index` of `4` is forced to `3`, even though `GoToSlide { index: 4 }` later treats slide 4 as valid via modulo wrapping. This also affects prop sync through the same last-page clamp, so controlled parents cannot select those wrapped positions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6F42  L1505  reply=3352246889 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Label the indicator tablist**

When indicators are rendered, this emits a bare `role="tablist"` with no accessible name. In the tabbed carousel pattern, screen-reader users need that group named (for example, “Choose slide”) to understand what the tabs control; otherwise the indicator set is announced only as a generic tablist. Add an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` message for `IndicatorGroup` rather than leaving the group unnamed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6F43  L693  reply=3352246892 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid trapping zero-duration carousels in Transitioning**

When a consumer passes `transition_duration: Some(Duration::ZERO)` to disable animation or honor reduced-motion styling, the context preserves that zero duration while navigation still enters `Transitioning` and waits for a `TransitionEnd`. Zero-duration CSS transitions commonly do not fire `transitionend`, so the machine can remain `Transitioning` indefinitely and reject subsequent navigation. Treat zero duration as an immediate settle or avoid the transition state in that configuration.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6F45  L1628  reply=3352246897 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not navigate from nested widget arrow keys**

If adapters attach this handler to the root as documented, keydown events bubbled from slide content also hit this match. In a carousel slide containing a text input, slider, or other keyboard widget, pressing ArrowLeft/ArrowRight is expected to edit or operate that child control, but this code dispatches carousel navigation instead. Scope the handler to the intended carousel controls or carry target metadata so nested interactive content can opt out.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

586	/// Returns `None` when `idx` equals the current index: the track transform
587	/// would not change, so the adapter has no CSS transition to report and
588	/// `TransitionEnd` may never arrive — entering `Transitioning` would strand
589	/// the machine and block all further navigation.
590	fn navigate_to(ctx: &Context, idx: usize) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
591	    if idx == ctx.current_index() {
592	        return None;
593	    }
594	    let stop = ctx
595	        .auto_play
596	        .as_ref()
597	        .is_some_and(|o| o.stop_on_interaction);
598	    let mut plan = TransitionPlan::to(State::Transitioning)
599	        .apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
600	            ctx.index.set(idx);
601	            if stop {
602	                ctx.auto_play_stopped = true;
603	            }
604	        })
605	        .with_effect(index_change_effect(idx));
606	    if stop {
607	        plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer);
608	    }
609	    Some(plan)
610	}
611	
612	/// Build the [`Effect::IndexChange`] notification carrying the newly requested
613	/// slide `index`. The adapter resolves it by invoking [`Props::on_index_change`]
614	/// — the round-trip path that lets a controlled parent observe navigation and
615	/// push the new index back through [`Props::index`].
616	fn index_change_effect(index: usize) -> PendingEffect<Machine> {
617	    PendingEffect::new(
618	        Effect::IndexChange,
619	        move |_ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {
620	            if let Some(callback) = &props.on_index_change {
621	                callback(index);
622	            }
623	            ars_core::no_cleanup()
624	        },
625	    )
626	}

1196	
1197	### 3.3 Screen Reader Announcements
1198	
1199	- `aria-live` on `ItemGroup` is `"off"` during auto-play to prevent disruptive announcements, and `"polite"` when paused or stopped.
1200	- Auto-play pauses on hover (`mouseenter` → `HoverStart`) when `AutoPlayOptions::pause_on_hover` is set, and on focus within the carousel (`focusin` → `FocusSlide`) when `pause_on_focus` is set. Each gate is enforced in the core, not the adapter. Rotation resumes on `mouseleave` / `focusout` (`HoverEnd` / `Blur`) unless permanently stopped. The auto-play trigger button's manual pause (`AutoPlayPause`) is unconditional and independent of these options.
1201	- Slides **outside the visible window** (`current_index` through `current_index + ceil(slides_per_view)`, wrapping when `loop_nav` is set) receive both `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert`, ensuring off-screen slides are invisible to assistive technology. With `slides_per_view > 1` every on-screen slide stays accessible — only the leading slide carries `data-ars-active`.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6avY  L814  reply=3352362559 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restart autoplay timer after swipe transitions**

When an autoplaying carousel is swiped with `stop_on_interaction: false`, `PointerDown` cancels `Effect::AutoPlayTimer` for the drag and the swipe path keeps it cancelled through the snap, but this `TransitionEnd` branch only changes the state back to `AutoPlaying` and never emits a replacement timer effect. The control and `data-ars-state` report that autoplay is playing, yet no interval is running, so rotation silently stops after the first swipe.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6avc  L1010  reply=3352362563 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore swipe releases while a transition is active**

When a user starts another drag before the current slide animation has sent `TransitionEnd`, this branch still accepts the `PointerUp` and can set a new index even though button/keyboard navigation is explicitly blocked during `State::Transitioning`. That lets rapid pointer input advance or skip slides mid-snap, contradicting the surrounding transition-blocking behavior and leaving adapters to reconcile overlapping animations.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6avf  L1678  reply=3352362567 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Send looped End key to the final slide**

With `loop_nav: true` and `slides_per_view > 1`, `last_index()` is the last non-looping contain-scroll page, not the final slide; for example 5 slides with 2 per view sends `End` to index 3 even though loop mode allows index 4 to be the leading slide. This makes the documented `End` = last slide keyboard behavior inconsistent with indicator/direct navigation in looped multi-view carousels.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6avg  L1142  reply=3352362568 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pause autoplay when focus enters controls**

The focus pause is only set from the slide-specific `FocusSlide` path, so keyboard focus on carousel controls such as Prev/Next, indicators, or the autoplay trigger has no core event/API path that sets `auto_play_paused_focus`. In the default `pause_on_focus` configuration, autoplay can keep advancing while a user is tabbing through those controls, even though the carousel contract says focus within the carousel pauses rotation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

1251:- Auto-play pauses on hover (`mouseenter` → `HoverStart`) when `AutoPlayOptions::pause_on_hover` is set, and on focus within the carousel (`focusin` → `FocusSlide`) when `pause_on_focus` is set. Each gate is enforced in the core, not the adapter. Rotation resumes on `mouseleave` / `focusout` (`HoverEnd` / `Blur`) unless permanently stopped. The auto-play trigger button's manual pause (`AutoPlayPause`) is unconditional and independent of these options.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6ud6  L1246  reply=3352473107 =====
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep autoplay timer running on same-state prop sync**

When `auto_play` is active and an unrelated prop changes, `target` is the current `State::AutoPlaying`, but `TransitionPlan::to(target)` still makes `SendResult.state_changed` true. The Leptos/Dioxus `use_machine` effect handlers drain all active effect cleanups on any state change, and because `auto_changed` is false this branch does not enqueue a replacement `AutoPlayTimer`; changing props such as `spacing`, `is_rtl`, or a controlled `index` while the carousel is steadily autoplaying therefore silently clears the interval while the machine still reports `AutoPlaying`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6ud7  L1235  reply=3352473108 =====
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep transitions active during autoplay prop sync**

When `SyncProps` arrives while the carousel is already `Transitioning`, changing or enabling `auto_play` makes `want_timer` true and this branch immediately targets `State::AutoPlaying`. A parent interval/config update during a slide snap therefore exits the transition before the adapter's `TransitionEnd`, allowing ticks or navigation to be accepted while the old CSS transition is still in flight; the sync should preserve `Transitioning` and reconcile the timer after the snap settles.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6ud8  L1273  reply=3352473109 =====
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the latest controlled index when releasing control**

When a controlled carousel receives a new controlled index and later switches to uncontrolled mode, `sync_controlled(None)` exposes the bindable's old internal value rather than the latest controlled value. For example, init with controlled `0`, set props to controlled `2`, then set props with `index: None` resets `current_index()` back to the stale internal `0`; seed the internal value from the last controlled index before clearing control so the visible slide does not jump.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

===== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6G6ud-  L795  reply=3352473111 =====
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp oversized GoToSlide indices without wrapping**

For an out-of-range `GoToSlide` target greater than `isize::MAX`, this cast wraps the `usize` to a negative `isize` before `clamp_index` sees it, so a non-looping carousel jumps to slide `0` instead of saturating to the last reachable slide as the spec/tests describe for out-of-range targets. Convert with a saturating path (or clamp as `usize`) before applying the signed helper; the same pattern should be avoided wherever public `usize` targets are fed through `as isize`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    /// Clamp or wrap an index according to `loop_nav`.\n    pub fn clamp_index(&self, i: isize) -> usize {\n        let n = self.slide_count.get() as isize;\n        if self.loop_nav {\n            ((i % n) + n) as usize % self.slide_count.get()\n        } else {\n            (i.max(0) as usize).min(self.last_index())\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Clamp/wrap an absolute `usize` target (direct `GoToSlide`/`FocusSlide`)\n    /// without routing through `as isize`, so a target above `isize::MAX`\n    /// saturates (non-loop) or wraps (loop) instead of overflowing negative.\n    pub fn clamp_index_usize(&self, index: usize) -> usize {\n        if self.loop_nav { index % self.slide_count.get() } else { index.min(self.last_index()) }\n    }\n"

value while\n                    // controlled) before clearing control, so releasing control\n                    // preserves it instead of revealing a stale internal.\n                    let displayed = ctx.current_index();\n                    let controlled = props.index.as_ref()\n                        .map(|bindable| (*bindable.get()).min(ctx.max_start_index()));\n                    ctx.index.sync_controlled(controlled);\n                    if !ctx.index.is_controlled() {\n                        ctx.index.set(displayed.min(ctx.max_start_index()));\n                    }\n                    if ctx.auto_play.is_none() {\n                        ctx.auto_play_paused_manual = false;\n                        ctx.auto_play_paused_hover = false;\n                        ctx.auto_play_paused_focus = false;\n                        ctx.auto_play_stopped = false;\n                    }\n                };\n                let mut plan = if changes_state {\n                    TransitionPlan::to(target).apply(apply)\n                } else {\n                    TransitionPlan::context_only(apply)\n                };\n                // Reconcile the timer to match `target`.\n                match target {\n                    State::AutoPlaying => {\n                        // (Re)arm when the state change drained effects or the\n                        // config changed; otherwise the interval is still running.\n                        if changes_state || auto_changed {\n                            plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer)\n                                .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::AutoPlayTimer));\n                        }\n                    }\n                    State::Idle => { plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer); }\n                    State::Transitioning => {\n                        // Stay in the snap; `TransitionEnd` re-arms on settle.\n                        if !want_timer { plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoPlayTimer); }\n                    }\n                }\n                Some(plan)\n            }"
}
